analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. The head hunk (lines 980-1027) adds a description of an ordinary EngineV2 startup shape warmup (ModelCalibrationPolicy.shapeWarmup). The two supplied units are BASE text for the file, lines 1-801, and do not include the changed region. I could only see the added patch excerpt, and it is truncated, so I cannot see the rest of the warmup description.

Security-relevant claims in the visible excerpt:
- Warmup runs once per loaded engine, before the calibration probes.
- It uses a greedy 128-token probe plus synthetic prompts.
- It has a 20-second wall budget.
- No rate or counter is trained.
- It uses the artifact's default sampling.

A warmup that submits synthetic prompts through the engine could touch the prefix cache (T-041) or the KV budget, and could affect availability. Because the change is documentation only, none of that is a code regression. Whether the implementation (ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift) isolates warmup from the SSD prefix cache and cache scopes, and from billing or receipts, cannot be verified from the supplied evidence. The doc does not state this, so the next pass should check it if the code is in scope. The doc text also does not claim a changed control.

The base text covers the Nemotron Super and GLM5Next serving docs. These are unchanged and I make no new claims about them. No threat-model assumption is invalidated by the visible hunk. No finding is raised. I set needs_deeper_review to false because the only residual question concerns code outside this documentation-only change.
